ICYMI O/N

IRAN:

Negotiating teams from the U.S. and Iran could return to Islamabad for peace talks later this week, four sources said to Reuters. Bloomberg sources also report the two sides "are weighing further negotiations to extend a two-week ceasefire", with the objective to hold fresh discussions before the truce announced April 7 expires next week. (RTRS/BBG)

US VP Vance said Monday that it is up to Iran to make the next move on peace talks with the U.S. "Whether we have further conversations, whether we ultimately get to a deal, I really think the ball is in the Iranian court, because we put a lot on the table," Vance said in a Fox News interview. (CNBC)

Saudi Arabia is pressing the U.S. to drop its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and return to the negotiating table, fearing President Trump’s move to close it off could lead Iran to escalate and disrupt other important shipping routes, Arab officials said to the WSJ. They warned Iran may close the Bab al-Mandeb Strait in response. (WSJ)

In a move designed to increase pressure on the US to make compromises in its conflict with his country, Iran foreign minister Araghchi has been briefing European capitals on the nature of the offer Iran had been willing to make about its stockpile of highly enriched uranium and future stewardship of the strait of Hormuz during the weekend talks in Islamabad. (Guardian)

Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi told his French counterpart that there had been progress in the negotiations with the US on many issues, although said that Iran was unable to reach an agreement because of constantly changing demands. (WSJ)

Iran's shadow fleet of tankers pose a challenge for the U.S. Navy, shipping experts say, setting up a potential game of cat and mouse as Washington attempts to enforce its blockade of Iranian ports. (WSJ)

Iranian oil sales in recent weeks have been favorable and part of the revenue will be allocated to repairing damage to industry caused by wartime attacks, Iran's oil minister said on Tuesday. (Jerusalem Post)

A U.S. blockade on Iranian ports is set to rapidly hit food imports to the Islamic republic, according to commodities provider Kpler. (WSJ)

South Korea has shared information with Iran on Korea-related ships stranded in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Yonhap sources, in a possible sign that Seoul may seek to negotiate their passage amid the U.S.-Iran war. (Yonhap)

US Secretary of State Rubio will take part in U.S.-brokered talks between Israel and Lebanon that are set to begin Tuesday in Washington, according to a State Department official. The discussions will involve the Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors to the U.S., with U.S. Ambassador to Lebanon Michel Issa also attending. (WSJ)

ENERGY CRISIS:

Global oil demand will decline this year for the first time since the 2020 pandemic as a price surge caused by the Middle East conflict wipes out growth, the International Energy Agency said. (BBG)

Chinese crude oil and natural gas imports fell in March, as the supply crunch in the Persian Gulf began to affect shipments. Crude purchases dropped 2.8% Y/Y to 49.982mln tons, although the figure was higher than February. Gas imports fell more sharply, down 11% to 8.183mln tons, leaving the YTD figure 4% below the pace set in 2025. Chinese oil product exports fell 12% to 4.601mln tons, after the government imposed curbs to conserve domestic fuel supplies. (BBG)

China’s lithium battery exports surged in the first quarter, reinforcing early signs of demand for alternative power sources to counter the global energy-supply crunch arising from the war in the Middle East. (BBG)

A hoard of Iranian crude on tankers at sea and robust onshore stockpiles in China will provide a cushion for the nation’s independent refiners should a US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz choke off flows. (BBG)

Major oil-producing countries in the Middle East have shown interest in using South Korea's crude oil storage facilities amid the prolonged conflict in their region, Seoul's senior industry ministry official said Tuesday. (Yonhap)

A prolonged Iran war could cause serious energy problems for the buildout of AI data centres, with a 10 to 20 per cent increase in total costs from an energy crunch potentially killing some projects. LNG and helium shortages risk crippling Asia's semiconductor supply chain and delaying AI infrastructure expansion, experts say. (SCMP)

The EU must strike a tricky balance between allowing countries to loosen spending to offset rising energy prices while avoiding a subsidy race, the EU’s incoming new antitrust chief tells the FT. (FT)

Europe’s biggest airlines are pushing the European Union to introduce temporary measures to help them through potential jet-fuel shortages and higher costs caused by the Iran war. (BBG)

The boss of Virgin Atlantic has warned that higher jet fuel prices are “here to stay” and cautioned that a prolonged war in the Middle East will hit global travel demand. He also said he can see about six weeks of secure jet-fuel supplies before the outlook get murkier. (FT/BBG)

Britain’s natural gas supply looks sufficient this summer despite the disruption to global energy flows caused by the Iran war, according to the grid manager. (BBG)

Western Australia will establish its own strategic reserves of diesel fuel to ease “acute shortages,” the state’s government said. (BBG)

Philippine economic managers rejected a halt in excise taxes on diesel and gasoline, saying a suspension won’t likely give meaningful relief to consumers from oil price swings due to the Iran war. (BBG)

MACRO:

The Federal Reserve should "wait and see" before deciding whether to lower interest rates amid the war in Iran, U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent told Semafor. (Semafor)

Fed's Miran said the energy shock triggered by the Iran war has yet to impact longer-run inflation expectations, and he expects price pressures to return to the central bank’s target in a year’s time. (BBG)

Corporate America is expected to deliver “exceptionally strong” first-quarter earnings, as a weak dollar and the Trump administration’s tax and spending plans help companies shrug off the fallout from war in the Middle East. (FT)

Investors are growing increasingly worried about US life insurers’ exposure to private credit, after many firms piled into the opaque asset class in an attempt to boost their investment returns. (FT)

A BlackRock Inc. private credit fund in Asia has suffered the first default by a borrower in its portfolio after a Chinese company failed to repay a loan, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

A Blue Owl Capital Inc. private credit fund raised $400 million from bond investors at 6.5% on Monday, marking the first deal of its kind in over a month, as worries about AI-disrupted software bets and looser lending standards have roiled the once red-hot industry. (BBG)

Citigroup Inc. strategists have joined Wall Street peers in turning more constructive on US stocks, saying elevated war uncertainty supports a preference for higher-quality and defensive companies. (BBG)

Trump has nominated a senior Pimco executive for a role at the US Treasury department negotiating with organisations such as the IMF at a time when the president is upending the global trade and economic order. (FT)

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has secured a majority government, cementing his hold on power after electoral victories Monday night and defections to his Liberal Party caucus over the past six months. (WSJ)

Japan’s 20-year government bond auction drew its strongest demand since 2019 as elevated yields attracted investors despite the continuing conflict in the Middle East. (BBG)

Corporate bond issuance in Japan is poised to breach a record this year on growing funding demand for mergers and acquisitions as the economy continues to move away from three decades of deflation. (BBG)

Japanese Finance Minister Katayama said she and PM Takaichi had told the trade minister to avoid commenting on the Bank of Japan's monetary policy, stressing decisions on policy tools should be left to the BOJ. (RTRS)

China’s export momentum slowed sharply in March, signaling the Middle East war is weighing on global demand and threatening a driver of growth. (WSJ)

China’s yuan will undergo a gradual process of internationalization that erodes the dollar’s dominance and, over the long run, become a more prominent global reserve currency, according to BNP Paribas Asset Management. (BBG)

China’s drive to turn the yuan into an international reserve currency is creating an opening and the next step should be matching regulatory requirements with international standards, said Euroclear Chief Executive Officer Valerie Urbain. (BBG)

China’s local governments have recently rolled out a range of incentives, from direct cash subsidies to interest-rate relief, in an effort to shore up the beleaguered property market, the Securities Daily reported. At least five cities, including Wuxi and Yichang, have unveiled new support measures since early April to lower entry barriers for buyers. (Securities Daily)

Chinese stocks are poised to gain 10% by year-end as Beijing’s supportive policies drive growth and valuations remain discounted, according to London-based asset manager Eurizon SLJ Capital. (BBG)

China’s lithium carbonate supply is facing a mounting squeeze as a regulatory cleanup in a key domestic hub coincides with export curbs in Zimbabwe. (Shanghai Securities News) 

Global borrowers are flocking to issue bonds in Hong Kong dollars as the currency’s status as a haven from the conflict in Iran bolsters demand for the securities. (BBG)

China and Spain pledged on Tuesday to deepen ties and safeguard global peace and development amid an international order that President Xi Jinping called "crumbling" in remarks during a meeting with Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez in Beijing. (RTRS)

ECB's Rehn said the Iran war will drive inflation higher this year but policymakers can’t commit to a path for borrowing costs. (BBG)

U.S. officials who met leaders of France's far-right National Rally were underwhelmed by their economic plans, two diplomatic sources said to Reuters, in a blow to the party's efforts to present itself as a credible steward of the euro zone's No. 2 economy before next year's election. (RTRS)

Surging fuel prices caused by the conflict in Iran weighed on British consumers last month, dampening household spending as travel plans were shelved, surveys showed on Tuesday. (RTRS)

British households and factories will be offered payments to use more electricity at certain times of the day in order to soak up surplus power supply, as grid operators grapple with the impact of more renewable energy sources. (FT)

Australia's business and consumer confidence crashed as the Iran war unleashed a global oil shock that may tip the local economy into a recession, separate surveys showed on Tuesday, as policymakers weigh if more rate rises are needed to tame inflation. (RTRS)

RBA's Hauser said Australia’s inflation remains too high and interest rates will need to be set at a level consistent with returning it to the 2–3% target, as a surge in energy prices tied to the Iran war sent consumer and business confidence tumbling. (BBG)

Polish central banker Ludwik Kotecki said he sees no room for further interest rate cuts this year due to uncertainty surrounding the war in the Middle East and its impact on inflation in Poland. (RTRS)

Singapore tightened its monetary policy settings in a widely expected move, becoming the first in Asia to respond to rising inflation risks stemming from a surge in energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict. (BBG)

Malaysia still has room to deploy fiscal support for industries impacted by the fallout of the Iran war, according to Zafrul Aziz, chair of the Malaysian Investment Development Authority. (BBG)

Argentina is expected to reach a staff-level agreement with the International Monetary Fund on the second review of its $20 billion program as early as this week, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG) 

Colombia is planning to repurchase some $4 billion of its bonds, according to public credit director Javier Cuellar. (BBG)

A German oil trader who made a $250mn profit trading Russian oil after Moscow’s assault on Ukraine is expanding in Guyana to tap into its multibillion-dollar oil boom. (FT)

GEOPOLITICAL:

'Russia’s war-driven tax squeeze pushes small businesses to the brink' FT article notes traders struggle to keep operating as Moscow raises VAT to 22% and slashes exemptions for SMEs. (FT)

Ukraine’s drone strikes on key Russian oil-export outlets in the Baltic and Black seas may put India’s crude-refining operations at risk in the near future, according to the International Energy Agency. (BBG)

More than 17,000 military personnel will participate in the biggest-ever joint drills by the Philippines, the US and other nations as they rehearse warfighting skills amid tensions with China and the Middle East conflict. (BBG)

EQUITIES:

OpenAI's $852 billion valuation is under scrutiny from some of its own backers as the company shifts its focus to the enterprise market to fend off competition from Anthropic, the Financial Times reported. Some investors said that the changes could leave it vulnerable to Anthropic and a resurgent Google. (FT)

SK Hynix is reportedly pursuing a plan to reduce its 6th-generation High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) shipments to NVIDIA by approximately 20–30% compared to its original plan. This is understood to be a consequence of NVIDIA's next-generation AI accelerator "Vera Rubin" facing difficulties in scaling mass production. The reduced HBM4 volumes from SK Hynix are expected to be substituted by demand for the previous-generation HBM3E and server DRAM. (ZDNet via @jukan05)

Oracle Corp. agreed to purchase as much as 2.8 gigawatts of fuel-cell power from Bloom Energy Corp. to supply data centers for artificial intelligence work. (BBG)

Microsoft Corp. raised prices sharply across its Surface-branded device lineup, becoming the latest personal computer maker to pass along costs fueled by a historic memory chip shortage. (BBG)

Novo Nordisk and OpenAI will work together as they seek to harness artificial intelligence to discover new drugs and improve efficiency. (WSJ)

United Airlines CEO Kirby pitched the potential for merging with American Airlines in a meeting with US President Trump in late February, according to Reuters sources, raising the prospect of an industry-reshaping deal likely to face significant regulatory hurdles. (RTRS)

A hacking group with a history of compromising major global corporations said it had stolen nearly 80 million business records from video game developer Rockstar Games, the maker of Grand Theft Auto. (RTRS)

Chevron signed two key agreements on Monday to expand operations at Venezuela's vast Orinoco Belt, including an asset swap adding an extra heavy crude area to its main project while returning an offshore gas field and a small crude area, executives and officials said at an event. (RTRS)

Data-center operator Digital Realty Trust Inc. plans to invest €2 billion ($2.3 billion) in Italy over the next five years as part of a Mediterranean-focused build-out in Europe. (BBG)

Microsoft Corp., the world’s biggest investor in carbon removal projects, rejected speculation that it is abandoning its efforts to build out the technology. (BBG)

The UK's NHS analytics official had made no secret of his concerns about Palantir’s Federated Data Platform, questioning the need for the technology after its rollout last year at the hospital where he works. (FT)

Delta Air Lines Inc. quietly scrubbed a pair of key environmental targets from its sustainability web page late last week. (BBG)

Chinese memory chipmaker Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC) aims to build two more factories in addition to one that will be completed this year, which will more than double its production capacity when all three are up and running, according to Reuters sources. The three new plants will each have the capacity to produce 100,000 wafers per month when fully operational. (RTRS)

The founder of China Evergrande Group, the world's most indebted property developer, pleaded guilty to charges including misuse of funds, fundraising fraud and illegally taking public deposits, a court in China's southern city of Shenzhen said. (RTRS)

Samsung’s union wants 15% of the company’s operating profit as a bonus. (Korean Herald via @dnystedt)

South Korean AI chip startup DeepX, an on-device AI chip company, which works with Hyundai Motor and Baidu, said on Tuesday it is preparing to list its shares domestically, adding the firm is open to a possible U.S. listing after that. (RTRS)

Nissan Motor Co. has unveiled a makeover of its aging lineup, setting ambitious targets to raise sales in the US and China a year after Chief Executive Officer Ivan Espinosa took charge of the ailing carmaker. (BBG)

Publicis Groupe said strong demand for services powered by artificial intelligence drove top-line growth in the U.S. and other key markets in the first quarter, offsetting a hit from the war in the Middle East. (WSJ)

BP said it expects an exceptional oil trading result for the first quarter, as the war in the Middle East fueled market volatility. (WSJ)

Imperial Brands said it expects to report higher adjusted operating profit for the first half of fiscal 2026, helped by strong tobacco pricing and revenue growth from its vaping, heated tobacco and oral nicotine products. (WSJ)

Antofagasta Plc is taking an early look at opportunities in Argentina as sweeping policy changes revive interest in one of the world’s most promising new copper frontiers, Chief Executive Officer Iván Arriagada said in an interview. (BBG)

China has lifted bans on procurement of the key steelmaking ingredient from mining giant BHP Group, sources told Reuters, ending a months-long dispute following a visit by the miner's top executives to its largest customer. (RTRS)

Australia’s Qantas Airways said its near-term jet fuel bill would be up to 32% more than previously anticipated, as the Iran conflict hits profitability in global aviation. (WSJ)

LOOK: Members of Filipinos Do Not Yield (FDNY), Alyansa Bantay Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (ABKD), Liga Independencia ng Pilipinas, and the People’s Alliance for Democracy and Reforms (PADER) stage a protest outside the House of Representatives in Quezon City on Tuesday, April 14, coinciding with the House Committee on Justice hearing on the impeachment complaint against Vice President Sara Duterte.

The groups urged lawmakers to push through with the impeachment, saying it is a legitimate constitutional tool for holding public officials accountable. | 📷: Grig C. Montegrande, Philippine Daily Inquirer
